title: The obtuse angle with the same sine as a given acute angle
source: Theory IGCSE-15.6 Quick check 2 (obtuse angle with sine equal to sin 30 is 150); related angle 180 minus acute, new special angles
stem: Find the obtuse angle, in degrees, whose sine is equal to \(\sin {p|int}^\circ\).

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: Sine is also positive in the second quadrant, so the obtuse angle is \(180^\circ-{p|int}^\circ={A|int}^\circ\).

title: Solve tan x = root 3 for 0 to 360 degrees

source.note: Stem taken from the QP PDF (UCLES 2021), Question 24, including the exact equation tan x = root 3 (verified on the official page, not the garbled pdftotext form). Official answer and mark allocation from the MS PDF. The item is paper/self-mark.

stem:
This question is 0580/23/O/N/21 Question 24, taken from the official QP.

\(\tan x=\sqrt{3}\) and \(0^\circ\leqslant x\leqslant 360^\circ\).

Find all the possible values of \(x\).  [2]

steps.name: B1
steps.note: Official MS 24: 60 and 240, 2 marks, B1 for 60 or 240. If 0 scored, SC1 for two answers with a difference of 180 degrees.

steps.name: B2
steps.text_tex: Tangent is also positive in the third quadrant, so the other solution in the interval is \(x=180^\circ+60^\circ=240^\circ\).
steps.note: Official MS 24: the second value is 240. Independent: 180+60=240, and tan(240)=tan 60=root 3.
